title: PCIe-style data link layer: TLP framing with sequence numbers and LCRC, Ack/Nak DLLPs with CRC-16, replay buffer and timer, flow-control init (InitFC1/InitFC2) and header credits, on a PIPE-like symbol interface

fields.desc: physical link up: starts flow-control init; clearing it drops the link (buffers and sequence numbers reset)

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: TLP byte to send; one write per byte, LAST on the final byte (a TLP is cut after MAXLEN = 32 bytes). The core takes bytes while the link is up and a replay-buffer slot is free

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Received TLP byte (head of the core's receive buffer); reading it pops it. TLPs are delivered once their LCRC and sequence number check out; header credits are returned as they are read

irqs.name: RETRAIN
irqs.desc: the fourth replay without progress: the physical layer should retrain

irqs.name: ERR_TLP
irqs.desc: a TLP failed (bad LCRC, bad EDB, framing, sequence number ahead): a Nak is sent

irqs.name: ERR_SEQ
irqs.desc: a TLP with a sequence number ahead of the expected one

irqs.name: TLP_DUP
irqs.desc: a duplicate TLP (already received): dropped and acknowledged

irqs.name: TLP_NULL
irqs.desc: a nullified TLP (EDB with inverted LCRC): dropped silently

irqs.name: ERR_OVERFLOW
irqs.desc: a good TLP with the receive buffer full: dropped, not acknowledged

irqs.name: ERR_PROTO
irqs.desc: a DLLP of unknown type, or an Ack/Nak with reserved bits or a sequence number never sent

irqs.name: ERR_FRAME
irqs.desc: a framing error (K symbol out of place, DLLP of the wrong length)

notes: tx_sym / tx_k and rx_sym / rx_k are the symbol interface (one 8-bit symbol per PCLK, K flag for STP FB, SDP 5C, END FD, EDB FE); they pass through unchanged.
The core parameters MAXLEN (32), TXN (4 replay slots), RXN (4 receive TLPs), REPLAY_TO (600), FC_GAP (32) and UPD_GAP (1024) keep their defaults.
